# Validator

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Formats` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public static class Validator
```

The single place that decides what a legal CookBook is.

It REPORTS problems and never throws, because `validate` — and a GUI asking "what is wrong with this book?" — exists precisely to explain a broken one. A validator that crashes on bad input fails at the only moment it matters.

## Methods

### Validate(LoadedCookBook) { #m-validate-nfty-core-formats-loadedcookbook }

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<string> Validate(LoadedCookBook cb);
```

Checks a book and returns every problem found, rather than stopping at the first.

**Parameters**

- `cb` (`LoadedCookBook`) - The book to check.

**Returns.** One human-readable line per problem; empty when the book is legal.

### ValidateIngredient(LoadedIngredient) { #m-validateingredient-nfty-core-formats-loadedingredient }

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<string> ValidateIngredient(LoadedIngredient ing);
```

Validates a standalone ingredient — every check that does NOT need a canvas. The canvas is a property of the CookBook, so "does this variant match the canvas?" cannot be answered here; [`Validator.Validate()`](Nfty.Core.Formats.Validator.md#m-validate-nfty-core-formats-loadedcookbook) remains the authoritative whole-book gate. Used by the CLI's `new ingredient` / `add variant`, which build an .igt before a canvas exists.

**Parameters**

- `ing` (`LoadedIngredient`)

### ValidateRecipe(LoadedRecipe) { #m-validaterecipe-nfty-core-formats-loadedrecipe }

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<string> ValidateRecipe(LoadedRecipe r);
```

Validates a standalone recipe — every canvas-independent check, plus that all variant images across all its ingredients share one size, so they could match some future canvas. Used by the CLI's `new recipe` / `add ingredient`.

**Parameters**

- `r` (`LoadedRecipe`)
